11822.name: JuicyPotato
11822.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]JuicyPotato, also known as juicypotato, is a privilege escalation tool. It exploits Windows vulnerabilities to escalate privileges, specifically using techniques like T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation) and T1021 (Remote Services) for lateral movement. It can be deployed as a web shell variant to execute arbitrary commands, such as spawning cmd.exe for a reverse shell. The tool is popular among Chinese-speaking threat actors and targets Windows platforms.[/profile]

11824.name: DeathNote
11824.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]DeathNote is a malware cluster that overlaps with the ThreatNeedle cluster and has been used to target the defense industry with job vacancy decoys. It is attributed to the Lazarus Group. Its technical behaviors include using Multi-Stage Channels for command and control, performing System Network Connections Discovery, and employing Archive Collected Data and Clipboard Data techniques for collection. Its associated locations include Cyprus, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and the United States of America.[/profile]

11825.name: Gopuram
11825.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Gopuram is a modular backdoor deployed with surgical precision, attributed to the Lazarus Group. It is delivered via supply chain compromise, specifically through trojanized 3CXDesktopApp installers for Windows and macOS. Its key technical behaviors include using multi-stage command and control channels and collecting clipboard data. The malware primarily targets cryptocurrency companies, with observed infections in locations including Cyprus, Hong Kong, France, Italy, and Germany, and has used domains like wirexpro.com and oilycargo.com for infrastructure.

11826.name: Operation DreamJob
11826.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Operation DreamJob is a malware operation attributed to the Lazarus Group. It employs Supply Chain Compromise for initial access, uses Multi-Stage Channels for command and control, and performs data collection via Clipboard Data and System Network Connections Discovery. Collected data is prepared for exfiltration using Archive Collected Data. The operation has targeted entities in locations including Cyprus, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and the United States.

11827.name: COPPERHEDGE
11827.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]COPPERHEDGE is a full-featured remote access tool (RAT) attributed to the Lazarus Group. It is capable of running arbitrary commands, performing system reconnaissance, and exfiltrating data. Key technical behaviors include collecting data from the clipboard, using multi-stage command and control (C2) channels, and archiving collected data prior to exfiltration. It has been associated with targets in locations including the United States, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Cyprus. A variant of this malware can be executed in memory.[/profile]

11829.name: Roaming Mantis
11829.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Roaming Mantis, also known as Wroba, is a malware attributed to the Roaming Mantis group. It primarily targets Android devices via DNS hijacking for initial access and uses multi-stage command and control channels. Its key behaviors include collecting clipboard data, archiving collected data for exfiltration, and discovering system network connections. Its activity has been observed in locations including Cyprus, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and the United States.[/profile]

11919.name: AppleJeus
11919.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]AppleJeus is a malware family attributed to the Lazarus Group. It employs phishing (T1566) for initial access, uses command and scripting interpreters (T1059) for execution, and can perform screen capture (T1113) for data collection. Its primary targets are cryptocurrency trading platforms, as indicated by associated applications like Celas Trade Pro, JMT Trading, Union Crypto, Kupay Wallet, CoinGoTrade, Dorusio, and Ants2Whale. Its command and control infrastructure has included domains such as telloo.io, strainservice.com, bloxholder.com, and rebelthumb.net.[/profile]

11968.name: QuiteRAT
11968.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]QuiteRAT is a remote access trojan (RAT) and an evolution of the bulkier MagicRAT malware family, averaging a smaller 4-5MB in size. It is attributed to the Silent Chollima group and has been observed targeting entities in Japan, North Korea, Canada, and the United States. Its key behaviors include using web services for command and control (C2), as evidenced by its C2 infrastructure (e.g., http://146.4.21.94/tmp/tmp/log.php), and leveraging remote services for lateral movement. Initial access is often gained through phishing, and it uses command and scripting interpreters for execution while attempting to subvert trust controls for defense evasion.[/profile]

11969.name: DeimosC2
11969.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]DeimosC2 is a malware entity. Its infrastructure includes C2 servers at IPs like 108.61.186.55:443 and 146.4.21.94, using web services for command and control. It employs TTPs such as T1553 (Subvert Trust Controls) for defense evasion, T1021 (Remote Services) for lateral movement, and T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter) for execution. It has been observed targeting systems in Japan, North Korea, Canada, and the United States.[/profile]

11971.name: CollectionRAT
11971.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]CollectionRAT is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) targeting users in Japan, South Korea, Canada, and the United States. Its initial access is facilitated through phishing campaigns. For command and control (C2), it uses a Web Service, communicating with specific infrastructure including domains like http://146.4.21.94/tmp/tmp/log.php and http://146.4.21.94/boards/boardindex.php. It employs a Command and Scripting Interpreter for execution and leverages Remote Services for lateral movement within a compromised network. The malware also utilizes the Subvert Trust Controls technique for defense evasion.[/profile]

12075.name: VSingle
12075.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]VSingle, also known as vsingle, is a malware attributed to groups including Lazarus Group, Silent Chollima, APT10, APT32, Anunak, and Gallium. It obtains command and control (C2) server information from GitHub. For persistence, it can create a Windows registry key to automatically launch a copy on system startup. Its associated techniques include Subvert Trust Controls, Modify Authentication Process, Develop Capabilities, Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts, and Supply Chain Compromise, with targeting linked to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and India.

12076.name: BianLian
12076.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]BianLian, also known as bianlian, is a malware with attributed groups unknown. Its key TTPs include Subvert Trust Controls, Modify Authentication Process, Develop Capabilities, Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts, and Supply Chain Compromise. Target platforms are not specified. Infrastructure includes IP addresses such as 66.29.155.44, 85.13.118.11, 87.247.185.109, 91.102.162.229, 94.131.98.34, 94.198.50.195, 103.57.250.152, 104.36.229.15, 104.194.11.252, 104.238.34.130, 104.238.35.163, 104.238.60.64, 104.238.61.150, 104.243.32.53, 104.243.33.83, 104.243.33.84, 108.174.60.151, 120.48.110.233, and 139.59.40.48.

12077.name: GREASE
12077.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]GREASE, also known as grease, is a malware attributed to the North Korean APT group Kimsuky. It is associated with the MITRE ATT&CK techniques Subvert Trust Controls (T1553), Modify Authentication Process (T1556), Develop Capabilities (T1587), Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts (T1037), and Supply Chain Compromise (T1195). Its operations have been linked to locations including the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and India.

12078.name: Acres
12078.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Acres is a malware entity. It is associated with the attack patterns Subvert Trust Controls (T1553), Modify Authentication Process (T1556), Develop Capabilities (T1587), Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts (T1037), and Supply Chain Compromise (T1195), indicating capabilities in defense evasion, credential access, persistence, and initial access. It has been geolocated to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and India.

12101.name: Five Eyes
12101.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Five Eyes is a malware entity. Its technical behaviors include Audio Capture via system APIs to record and exfiltrate audio, Access Token Manipulation using Windows APIs to escalate privileges, and Impair Defenses by modifying security settings and logging. It establishes persistence via Boot or Logon Autostart Execution. Associated infrastructure indicators include domains such as icimp.swarkul.com, beeztrend.com, merudlement.com, speclaurp.com, and tarzoose.com. It is referenced in context discussing China's publications on Five Eyes operations and international law enforcement forums.[/profile]

12102.name: MATA
12102.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]MATA, also known as Dacls, is a malware attributed to the Lazarus Group. Its key technical behaviors include using Audio Capture (T1123) to record audio for exfiltration, Impairing Defenses (T1562) to disable security tools, manipulating Access Tokens (T1134) for privilege escalation, Creating Accounts (T1136) for persistence, and performing Account Discovery (T1087). It targets Windows and Linux platforms, utilizing infrastructure such as domains like speclaurp.com, myballmecg.com, merudlement.com, beeztrend.com, and prajeshpatel.com.[/profile]

12104.name: MataDoor
12104.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]MataDoor is a malware that establishes persistence via Boot or Logon Autostart Execution (T1547), such as creating a Windows Registry key. It performs defense evasion through Access Token Manipulation (T1134) and Impair Defenses (T1562), and conducts discovery via Account Discovery (T1087). It also has Audio Capture (T1123) capabilities. Its known command-and-control infrastructure includes domains like speclaurp.com, icimp.swarkul.com, zawajonly.com, myballmecg.com, and merudlement.com.[/profile]

12105.name: Lamberts
12105.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Lamberts is a sophisticated malware, also known as GRAYFISH, and is considered the rootkit of the Equation Group. It functions as a stage 2 payload for the 32-bit version of the Regin malware, specifically the "In Registry" variant, and is also referred to as white Lamberts (with black Lamberts being the 64-bit Regin). It achieves persistence and privilege escalation via Boot or Logon Autostart Execution, such as creating Windows Registry keys. For defense evasion and privilege escalation, it employs Access Token Manipulation and Impair Defenses techniques. It performs Audio Capture to record audio for collection. Its known infrastructure includes domains like icimp.swarkul.com, zawajonly.com, prajeshpatel.com, speclaurp.com, and mbafleet.com.[/profile]

12106.name: Linux MATA
12106.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Linux MATA, also known as Dacls, is a malware attributed to the Lazarus Group. It employs techniques such as Boot or Logon Autostart Execution for persistence and Impair Defenses to disable security mechanisms. The malware targets Linux platforms and uses C2 infrastructure including domains like speclaurp.com, merudlement.com, myballmecg.com, tarzoose.com, and beeztrend.com.[/profile]

12132.name: Scout
12132.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Scout, also known as the first stage of RCS, is a malware attributed to groups including Hacking Team and APT-C-34. It performs initial checks and AV-bypassing tricks, installs itself, and verifies no other instances are running. Its key TTPs include Boot or Logon Autostart Execution for persistence via registry keys, and techniques like Impair Defenses and Indicator Removal for defense evasion. It is deployed as part of a multi-stage process, preceding the Soldier or Elite payloads.[/profile]

12134.name: Volgmer
12134.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Volgmer is a backdoor Trojan malware family used by the Lazarus Group (also known as HIDDEN COBRA) since at least 2013 to target government, financial, automotive, and media sectors. Its key behaviors include establishing persistence via boot or logon autostart execution (T1547), conducting network service discovery (T1046), and employing defense evasion through indicator removal (T1070) and impairing defenses (T1562). It is typically delivered via phishing (T1566) and is designed to provide covert access to compromised systems.[/profile]

12163.name: T1150
12163.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]T1150, also known as Plist Modification, is a persistence technique for macOS and OS X platforms. It involves adversaries modifying property list (plist) files, which are XML-like configuration files located in directories such as /Library/Preferences or ~/Library/Preferences. By altering these files, attackers can point system or application execution to their own malicious code, enabling execution in another user's context, bypassing security whitelists, and establishing persistence, as demonstrated by threats like the Sofacy Komplex Trojan.

12165.name: T1495
12165.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The entity is the MITRE ATT&CK technique T1495, known as Firmware Corruption, which falls under the Impact tactic. It targets platforms including Windows, Linux, macOS, and Network Devices. This technique involves adversaries overwriting or corrupting the flash memory contents of system BIOS or other firmware in attached devices to render them inoperable or unable to boot, thereby denying availability. For instance, corrupting the firmware responsible for loading the operating system on network devices can cause a persistent denial of service. This attack can also lead to related effects like Data Destruction.

12167.name: Firmware Corruption
12167.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]Firmware Corruption is identified as MITRE ATT&CK technique T1495 under the Impact tactic, targeting macOS, Linux, Windows, and Network Devices. This technique involves adversaries overwriting or corrupting the flash memory contents of system BIOS or other firmware on attached hardware devices, such as motherboards, hard drives, or video cards. The primary objective is to render these devices or the entire system inoperable or unable to boot, thereby denying availability. For instance, corrupting the firmware responsible for loading the operating system on network devices can permanently disable them, which may also lead to associated data destruction.

12169.name: LPEClient
12169.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]LPEClient is a profiling malware used by the Lazarus Group, specifically within its ThreatNeedle and Bookcode clusters. It has been employed in attacks targeting South Korea's defense industry. Its technical behaviors are associated with standard Command and Control techniques like Data Encoding (T1132) and Encrypted Channel (T1573), as well as persistence mechanisms like Boot or Logon Autostart Execution (T1547). Its infrastructure involves C2 servers communicating via HTTP and HTTPS, with observed indicators including domains like api.shw.kr, theorigin.co.kr, and ictm.or.kr.[/profile]

12171.name: SIGNBT
12171.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]SIGNBT is a malware that uses T1132 (Data Encoding) and T1573 (Encrypted Channel) for command and control, employing standard encoding and encryption to obfuscate its traffic. It establishes persistence via T1547 (Boot or Logon Autostart Execution) by creating a registry key for automatic startup. Its infrastructure includes C2 servers hosted on domains like pms.nninc.co.kr, www.medric.or.kr, and www.vietjetairkorea.com. The malware is delivered through T1195 (Supply Chain Compromise) and can move laterally using T1021 (Remote Services) such as RDP and SSH, primarily targeting Windows systems.[/profile]

12249.name: SoulSearcher
12249.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]SoulSearcher, also known as soulsearcher, is a custom malware attributed to the SharpPanda threat group. It uses a DLL payload loaded from the Windows Registry for persistence (T1547) and employs Multi-Stage Channels (T1104) for command and control, utilizing infrastructure such as the domain office.oiqezet.com. Its behaviors include using Native API (T1106) for execution and Indicator Removal (T1070) for defense evasion. The malware has been used in espionage campaigns targeting Southeast Asia, specifically Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam, and is delivered via spearphishing (T1566).[/profile]

12250.name: Sharp Panda
12250.profile_without_enhance_5: [profile]The intrusion set is most likely the APT group known as Sharp Panda, also known as Sharp Dragon. Its key custom malware is SoulSearcher, which uses Windows Registry persistence (T1547) and multi-stage C2 channels (T1104) via infrastructure like office.oiqezet.com. Its TTPs include defense evasion via indicator removal (T1070) and execution via Native API (T1106), with initial access achieved through spearphishing (T1566). The group is attributed to China and has conducted espionage campaigns targeting Southeast Asia, specifically Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam, with a primary motivation of intelligence gathering.[/profile]
